clue.text: In this case, the object of the action is made clear

definitions.text: In this case, the object of the action is made clear

blocks.clueFragment: In this case, the object of the action is made clear
blocks.note: surface reading: a lawyer explaining what a lawsuit is about

blocks.clueFragment: In this case, the object of the action
blocks.note: setter's reading: a grammatical case, the one that marks the direct object of a verb

explanation.surface: A lawyer sets out what a particular lawsuit is aiming at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' and 'action' sound legal, but the case is grammatical and the object is the object of a verb. The legal flavour also echoes 'accuse'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin and German grammar the accusative is the case used for a verb's direct object.

clue.text: Split by an old quarrel in Switzerland

definitions.text: Split by an old quarrel in Switzerland

blocks.clueFragment: Split by an old quarrel in Switzerland
blocks.note: surface reading: a Swiss community divided by an ancient feud
setter's reading: the fruit William Tell shot an arrow through on his son's head, in Swiss legend, during his quarrel with the tyrant Gessler

explanation.surface: Some Swiss village is divided by a long-running feud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' looks like 'divided', but it is literal: the arrow split the fruit. William Tell is the Swiss folk hero forced to shoot it from his son's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says Tell's arrow cleft the fruit balanced on his boy's head, so that fruit was split in Switzerland.

clue.text: Resumed unnoticed movement

indicators.note: movement suggests letters shifting about from their places into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Some activity started again without anyone spotting it.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on after a pause is to take something up again, so the two past-tense verbs match.

clue.text: The _prince's rotten country?-

blocks.note: surface reading: some prince ruling a corrupt land
setter's reading: Hamlet's homeland, where Marcellus says something is rotten

explanation.walkthrough: The prince is Hamlet, and the line is 'Something is rotten in the state of Denmark' from Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is Prince of Denmark, and Marcellus's famous line calls that kingdom's condition rotten.

clue.text: Metal support for article - jolly hot

blocks.note: the definite article
a Jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A metal bracket holding up some item has become very hot.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the metal 'supports' the rest by sitting beneath it, so it comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermal means relating to heat, as in thermal underwear or a thermal spring that is naturally warm.

clue.text: Dances without one's bags!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the dances wrap around what follows

blocks.note: valse is the French word for waltz
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone goes dancing having left their luggage behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as 'lacking', but here it means outside, and the 's stands for 'has', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Valises are small travelling cases, so they are bags in the luggage sense.

clue.text: Swimmer in underwear abandoning the lake

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving something behind, so the named part is dropped

blocks.note: women's underwear
Lake Erie, one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A bather in underwear has left the lake behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' is crossword shorthand for a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The ling is a long, slender sea fish of the cod family, so a swimmer in crossword terms.

clue.text: Arab terrorists question one finally

blocks.note: the Irish Republican Army
Q is the abbreviation for question
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An Arab man is questioned by a terrorist group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' just tells you the one goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Iraq is an Arab national of that Middle Eastern country.

clue.text: Sponsor of the drag turn-out

indicators.note: a turn-out is a showing or outfit, and turning things out upsets their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone backs a drag act's show.
explanation.definitionFit: A godparent formally sponsors a child at baptism, vouching for their religious upbringing.

clue.text: Domesticated by marriage, according to Stevenson

definitions.text: Domesticated by marriage, according to Stevenson

blocks.note: surface reading: a man tamed by his wedding
setter's reading: R.L. Stevenson wrote that to marry is to domesticate the heavenly scribe who notes every sin

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is from Stevenson's essay collection Virginibus Puerisque: 'to marry is to domesticate the Recording Angel'.
explanation.definitionFit: In religious lore this angel writes down every person's good and bad deeds, and Stevenson joked that a spouse becomes one.

clue.text: Know how to reverse in long boat

indicators.note: to reverse is to go backwards, so the phrase is read from its end
in places the turned phrase inside the next word

blocks.note: to pine is to long for
to be able to do something

explanation.surface: Someone can back up a longboat.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed phrase goes between PIN and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnace is a small ship's boat, rowed or sailed, carried by a larger vessel.

clue.text: General drawback of islands

definitions.note: the answer is the name of a Caribbean island group

indicators.note: back tells you to read the word draw the other way

blocks.note: Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general
the word draw, followed by its own signal to read it the other way

explanation.surface: A military commander considers the disadvantage of fighting on islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawback' looks like one word meaning snag, but it splits into draw plus a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leeward Islands are a Caribbean chain, so the word names one particular group of islands.

clue.text: Skin deep inner grime is concealed

indicators.note: inner asks for the inside of the word that follows, dropping its first and last letters
concealed in the sense of disguised, and disguised letters are rearranged out of recognition

blocks.note: taken as written
the middle three of its five letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Dirt lies hidden just below the surface of the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skin deep' reads as one phrase, but the definition is Skin alone. 'Concealed' is an unusual anagram signal: read it as disguised.
explanation.definitionFit: The epidermis is the outer layer of the body's covering, over the dermis, so it names skin.

clue.text: Bilingual agreement on the DOWN board

blocks.note: yes in French
yes in German
a stray column heading picked up from the scanned page, not part of the clue

explanation.surface: A deal in two languages is agreed at board level.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised DOWN is a stray heading from the scanned page, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ouija board is the lettered board used at seances to spell out messages from spirits.

clue.text: Material given to the troops?

blocks.note: first meaning: cloth, especially woollen fabric
second meaning: an old word for military stores and supplies

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the less familiar sense: supplies issued to soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means woven fabric, and in older usage also an army's provisions, baggage and munitions.

clue.text: Decorated so-called cocktail with top of pineapple

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up
the top of a word in a down clue is where it begins

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A cocktail garnished with a slice of pineapple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So-called' looks like a sneer at the cocktail but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalloped edge is trimmed with a row of curves, so the word means ornamented in that way.

clue.text: Endure defeat in the final resort

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, as in a last-ditch attempt, describing a final resort

blocks.note: to last is to hold out or survive
to ditch can mean to thwart or scupper

explanation.surface: Someone holds out against defeat at a final stronghold.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from fighting to the last ditch, the final line of defensive trenches.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-ditch effort is a desperate one made when every other option has gone, which is what a final resort is.

clue.text: Fixed so-called pegs to the lines of washing

indicators.note: so-called means named or spoken of that way, pointing to how a word is said

blocks.note: fixed with a knot, said the same as the sea's rise and fall
pegs are markers used to record a level or score

explanation.surface: Someone pegs clothes on to the washing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines of washing' sounds like a clothes line; it means the grimy rings left by washing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidemarks are the dirty rings left round a bath, or the line between washed and unwashed skin on a neck.

clue.text: Count up the notes, then visit the official receiver

blocks.note: to total figures
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale, here pluralised
to see someone is to visit them

explanation.surface: A bankrupt tallies their banknotes before calling on the official who takes over their affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The official receiver is the British officer who handles bankruptcies; here the receiver is simply whoever a letter is sent to.
explanation.definitionFit: The person a letter or parcel is directed to formally receives it, so is its recipient.

clue.text: Australian vagrant, usually loaded

blocks.note: surface reading: a tramp who is, oddly, normally rich or drunk
setter's reading: an outback tramp who always carries his bundle of belongings

explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaded' suggests rich or drunk; it simply means carrying a load. A swag is the bedroll an Australian tramp carries, as in Waltzing Matilda.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia an itinerant worker or tramp who carries his bedroll on his back is named after that bundle.

clue.text: Hold fast to measure the length of a cricket pitch

blocks.note: an en is a printer's unit of measure

blocks.clueFragment: the length of a cricket pitch
blocks.note: a chain is 22 yards, exactly the distance between the wickets

explanation.surface: Someone is told to pace out a cricket pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: A chain is an old British surveying length of 22 yards, the same as a cricket pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: To bind someone with fetters is to secure them firmly, so it means to hold fast.

clue.text: Resolution to drain the depths

indicators.note: a resolution breaks something down into parts and resolves it into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A plan is agreed to empty out a deep pit.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest point of anything, like the worst moment of a career, is its bottom or depths.

clue.text: Plant in chimney surround

indicators.note: surround says one word goes round the other

blocks.note: lum is the Scots word for a chimney
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plant is growing in the fireplace surround.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word, but it is the letters that go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Linum is the botanical genus of flax, a flowering plant grown for linen and linseed.

clue.text: Back shortly, bearing rope's end

indicators.note: back says to read the word for shortly from right to left

blocks.note: before long
east, a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Someone will return soon carrying the end of a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop with a running knot is tied at the end of a rope, as on a lasso or gallows.

clue.text: One who applauds the champion royal title-holder

definitions.text: One who applauds the champion royal title-holder

blocks.note: surface reading: a fan cheering a sporting champion
setter's reading: one who hails a monarch, formally proclaiming them king or queen

explanation.walkthrough: To acclaim also means to declare someone ruler by public applause, so the cheering fan is also crowning a king.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hails or cheers enthusiastically, or proclaims a new sovereign by acclamation, is the noun formed from that verb.

clue.text: Redecorated nearly half the disco in colour

indicators.note: nearly half keeps a little under half of the word, cutting the rest
in places the cut word inside the colour

blocks.note: a primary colour
taken as written

explanation.surface: Half the disco has nearly been repainted in a new colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Two letters of five is nearly half.
explanation.definitionFit: To redecorate a room is to have done it all over again, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: American schedule for putting on a little weight

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
a gram is a small unit of mass

explanation.surface: An American diet plan for gaining a few pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' signals the US spelling, without the British -me ending.
explanation.definitionFit: A program in US spelling is a planned timetable of events, so a schedule.

clue.text: Advertisement about Green movement makes one cross

definitions.note: the answer is a past tense, meaning made someone cross

indicators.note: movement shifts the letters out of their order
about means round, so the notice wraps round the shifted colour

blocks.note: the short form
taken as written

explanation.surface: A campaign advert for the environmental movement upsets people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green movement' reads as the environmental lobby, but movement is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Making someone cross is to provoke their temper, which is what angered means.

clue.text: Performance held inside, due to bad weather

indicators.note: held inside says the letters sit within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across these two words
surface padding to complete the picture

explanation.surface: A show is moved indoors because of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece for two singers or players is a musical performance, the pair's turn on stage.

clue.text: Free, single in Paris, and careful in the extreme

indicators.note: in sets the careful word inside the word for extreme

blocks.note: un is French for one
the far limit of something
close means careful with money, stingy

explanation.surface: A single, careful person in Paris is free.
explanation.definitionFit: Land or an animal that is not fenced in or shut away is free and open.
